10.1002_adma.202510516: Electric, spin, and dipole coupling effects are increasingly employed in lithium–sulfur (Li─S) batteries to suppress the shuttle effect and enhance reaction kinetics. However, the controllable modulation of the electric field, spin states, and dipole interactions and their effects on lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) remains not fully understood, especially the synergies between these factors. Herein, we deliberately incorporates amorphous CoB specifically into Co‐CoP heterojunctions to coordinately regulate built‐in electric fields (BIEF), spin states, and electrostatic coupling effects. The amorphous CoB phase effectively reduces the BIEF intensity of Co‐CoP, facilitating bidirectional LiPSs migration across the heterointerface during the charging/discharging process. The doping of B induces the spin state of transition metal Co toward a low‐spin configuration, which leads to increased localization of d‐orbital electrons, reduces the d‐p energy level gap, and optimizes d‐p orbital hybridization between cobalt and sulfur atoms validated by theoretical calculations. Compared to the weak dipole moment in CoP, the uniform alignment of dipoles within CoB generates moderately enhanced electrostatic attraction, which enhances bonding effects with LiPSs and improves adsorption‐hybridization performance. This work proposes a multi‐dimensional cooperative regulation mechanism (BIEF, spin, and dipole) for enhancing the polysulfide confinement/conversion, which can be extended to other battery systems suffering from shuttle effects.
10.1002_adma.202519267: Defects at the buried interface represent a critical challenge that impedes further improvements in both the performance and scalable manufacturing of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Defect formation, lattice mismatch, and energy-level misalignment at this interface aggravate nonradiative recombination and accelerate photothermal degradation, thereby limiting both efficiency and operational stability. Here, we employ interface engineering using multifunctional molecules to suppress defect formation. To minimize redundant material screening, we combine theoretical calculations with experimental validation to identify 4-aminobutylphosphonic acid (4-ABPA) for modifying the interface between the perovskite layer and the electrode. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate 4-ABPA as a multifunctional molecular bridge that simultaneously anchors to the charge transport layer and interacts with the perovskite lattice. And its role in dynamically regulating perovskite crystallization and enhancing interfacial performance is uncovered. The dual-site chemical binding regulates crystallization, alleviates residual stress, suppresses interfacial defects, and optimizes energy-level alignment at the buried interface. As a result, voltage loss is reduced to 31 mV, enabling power conversion efficiencies of 25.56% in n-i-p and 26.45% in p-i-n architectures with negligible hysteresis. The modified devices also exhibit outstanding durability, retaining 83.91% of their initial performance under 1440 h of continuous operation and 91.59% after 2600 h of ambient storage. Our work establishes a systematic and universal buried-interface engineering strategy to further enhance efficiency and stability, thereby advancing the mass production of perovskite devices.
10.1002_advs.78095: The shuttling effect and sluggish conversion kinetics of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) hinder the further advancement of lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries, exhibiting high barriers. Among catalysts, single-atom catalysts (SACs) can accelerate LiPSs redox kinetics by leveraging M-S coordination, interfacial charge transfer, and anchoring effect of coordinating heteroatoms. Numerous researches have reported improved catalytic activity via screening central metal and coordinating atoms as well as optimizing coordination configurations. However, systematic summary concerning the principles in screening and design of asymmetric coordination structures, the evolution mechanisms of orbital hybridization and spatial geometry, and the corresponding structure-activity relationships governing LiPSs conversion kinetics remain unknown. In this review, we systematically summarize the modifications brought by asymmetric coordination chemistry and dual-atom coordination structures in terms of geometric configuration engineering, molecular orbital hybridization, and interfacial charge rearrangement, together with the underlying mechanisms for boosting LiPSs conversion kinetics. Centered on theoretical calculations supplemented by experimental validations, we elaborate the critical significance of asymmetric coordination chemistry of SACs in elevating the catalytic efficiency. Finally, the future developments of SACs in Li─S batteries are outlooked and prospected.
10.1002_anie.3363298: Electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) of lignin‐derived guaiacol offers an appealing route toward sustainable chemical production but is impeded by the exceptional stability of aromatic rings. Conventional rhodium catalysts with electronically symmetric Rh 0 –Rh 0 sites generally activate guaiacol through Rh 0 ‐arene π interactions. However, the induced electronic perturbation remains largely delocalized over the arene π system, resulting in only limited local polarization and sluggish dearomatizing hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we introduce a hydroxyl‐directed activation strategy that exploits the phenolic hydroxyl group as an intrinsic handle for aromatic‐ring activation. Spatially adjacent Rh 0 and Rh δ+ sites (Rh 0 –Rh δ+ ) were constructed in RhO x clusters through lattice‐oxygen‐mediated electrochemical reconstruction. The electron‐deficient Rh δ+ sites selectively anchor the phenolic hydroxyl group, perturbing resonance donation from the phenolic oxygen into the aromatic ring and inducing asymmetric redistribution of aromatic π‐electron density. This hydroxyl‐directed adsorption simultaneously orients the aromatic ring toward neighboring Rh 0 sites, thereby promoting d→π* back‐donation and lowering the hydrogenation barrier. The resultant Rh 0 –Rh δ+ catalyst achieves a 2‐methoxycyclohexanol production rate of 197.51 mmol h −1 g Rh −1 , which is 22‐fold higher than that of Rh 0 –Rh 0 . Our findings establish hydroxyl‐directed aromatic‐ring activation as an effective strategy for overcoming aromatic inertia, providing a design principle for the electrocatalytic upgrading of lignin‐derived aromatics.
10.1016_j.cej.2026.180812: Aquaculture wastewater frequently contains residual antibiotics (i.e., tetracycline, TC) and microbiological pathogens (i.e., Enterococcus faecalis ), posing environmental and health risks. While UVA-based advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) using emerging oxidants such as performic acid (PFA) and periodate (PI) remain unexplored for aquaculture water treatment despite promising performance. This study evaluated UVA/PFA and UVA/PI for simultaneous E. faecalis and TC removal across simulated (SW) and real aquaculture water (RW), assessing temperature and pH effects, reactive species, phytotoxicity, and bacterial regrowth. Optimal performance occurred at pH 8, matching aquaculture conditions, at operationally optimal doses (0.02 mM PFA vs. 2.50 mM PI; 125-fold molar difference). UVA/PFA reached 81% TC removal under low COD conditions, and 4.52 ± 0.21-log E. faecalis reduction in 5 min under high COD conditions. Meanwhile, UVA/PI achieved complete removal of both TC and E. faecalis : 100% TC removal and 4.40 ± 0.16-log E. faecalis reduction (15 and 60 min under low and high COD conditions, respectively). However, TOC-based mineralization remained limited (9–20%). Scavenger studies indicated predominance of oxidant-derived reactive species for UVA/PI (IO 4 • /IO 3 • ) and non-HO • radical species for UVA/PFA. UVA/PI showed toxicity toward Solanum lycopersicum L. and high turbidity in RW (401 NTU), not observed with UVA/PFA. No E. faecalis regrowth occurred over 2 weeks with UVA/PI, whereas UVA/PFA exhibited matrix-dependent variability and oxidant instability. UVA/PFA offers dose-efficient disinfection for low-organic load aquaculture systems, while UVA/PI provides robust performance across variable conditions. These results are proof-of-concept and require further validation, particularly ecotoxicity assessment, before scale-up in aquaculture systems can be considered.
